decisive_items: High-intensity areas in bilateral lenticular nucleus with lentiform fork sign
response.rationale: R4 (Leigh syndrome) is the champion due to the presence of high-intensity areas in bilateral lenticular nucleus with lentiform fork sign on T2-weighted brain MRI and a lactate peak on MRS, which are characteristic of Leigh syndrome. R5 (Mitochondrial disease) is the runner-up as it also has some supporting evidence, but it is less specific than R4.

rejected.why: Normal dopamine transporter scan contradicts Parkinson's disease diagnosis
Normal vitamin B1 levels contradict Wernicke's encephalopathy diagnosis
Less specific evidence compared to R4 and R5
Append-only completion with less specific evidence compared to R4
